positive: Many Samsung Fold owners say they are happy with their phones, while also admitting Apple's foldable looks impressive and welcoming it to the category.
Several commenters say Samsung has offered foldables for years and see Apple's entry as validating the category and pushing Samsung to improve.
Apple Pencil support is seen as a point where Samsung falls short. Some want stylus support and water resistance back on Samsung's folds.
negative: Many commenters say Apple's foldable copies ideas Samsung introduced years ago, and that Apple gets praise for features Samsung had long offered.
Some criticise Samsung's foldables for durability, with screens failing after about a year, plus buggy software and tradeoffs like weaker cooling to make devices thinner.
Others find the Apple device too small and heavy next to Samsung's, and joke that the price is out of reach.

positive: Many commenters are impressed that the crease is barely visible or not noticeable at all, and treat it as a major improvement.
The matte inner display is widely praised, both for how it looks and because it likely helps hide the crease.
negative: Many dislike the matte, textured inner display, saying it looks washed out, grainy or color-inaccurate compared with a glossy OLED, and suspect it mainly hides the crease.
Commenters are split on the inner camera: several prefer an under-display camera despite weaker quality, while others say it looked poor and was abandoned.

positive: Even Samsung fans and people uninterested in foldables admit the animation is impressive, and some call it a major selling point.
The effect that makes the front panel look see-through is singled out, and some note that it responds to the hinge angle, which could open possibilities for developers.
negative: Many commenters say the price is far too high, especially given everyday living costs, and some say it is more expensive still in their own countries.
Praising the folding animation as a headline feature comes across as underwhelming, and some see it as a simple visual effect with little substance.
Some worry about expensive repairs and a weaker dust and water resistance rating, and some say Samsung offers better value with discounts.

positive: Many commenters plan to swap a current Pro model for the Duo, saying it feels new and more exciting than a routine Pro upgrade.
Larger screen in a pocketable form is the main draw, with several hoping it reduces how often they carry a tablet or laptop.
Some argue the Duo's camera trade-offs are acceptable for non-professional use, since it was never pitched as a Pro and its price reflects the foldable display.
negative: Many commenters see the Duo's price as too high, especially when it brings camera compromises compared with a Pro or Pro Max.
The weaker cameras and missing Face ID are the main dealbreakers, and several current Pro owners see the Duo as a downgrade.
Some are choosing the 18 Pro or Pro Max, or waiting for a later Duo, citing unknowns, limited need for the inner screen and an existing iPad.

positive: Several left-handed commenters say they would adapt to the layout and still want the phone, with no real objection to using it.
Viewers like the button and toolbar placement, saying it suits pockets, one-handed screenshots and keeps screen space free when unfolded.
Many see the half-folded and unfolded sizes as practical for gaming, navigation and medical reading, and several say they plan to buy one.
negative: Left-handed users feel the design disregards them and expect it to be awkward or frustrating for their hand.
The device's weight, width and added case thickness are seen as making one-handed use difficult.
Some say the folded form is awkward to hold and that interface elements near the hinge are poorly placed.

positive: Many commenters say they intend to buy the foldable, citing long-held interest in a folding phone and excitement about Apple's take on it.
Some see it as a phone-plus-tablet replacement, appealing to people with older iPad minis or who want to carry fewer devices.
Several accept trade-offs like a weaker camera or Touch ID, valuing the software, screen size and design more; one cites a cheaper rival.
negative: Many commenters say the price is far too high and out of reach for most people, with jokes about loans and financing.
Some question whether the cost is justified, noting weaker cameras than Pro models and limited storage for what is asked.
Others doubt the foldable design and features are new or useful enough, citing durability, comfort and bulk concerns.

positive: Many commenters express strong excitement and eagerness to buy or pre-order the foldable iPhone Duo, with some saying they have waited a long time for one.
Commenters praise the design and polish, including the premium materials, smooth open and close transition, and the practical benefit of multitasking on a phone.
Some Android users and former skeptics say the Duo won them over, while others note foldables are not new technology.
negative: Many commenters see the foldable as overpriced and heavy, and say they would wait for a later generation once Apple has refined it.
Commenters doubt the first-generation foldable screen will hold up, and think it may break or be left out of the full picture until teardown tests.
Several say Apple lacks fresh ideas and holds back features to impress people later, so they are not excited and see no need to fold.

positive: Many commenters say companies borrowing ideas from each other benefits consumers, and that Apple's polish and design set its version apart.
Commenters praise the build quality, software experience and looks, with some saying the design won over their initial skepticism.
Many loyal Apple users say they plan to buy it at launch, and a few Android users are considering switching.
negative: Many commenters say Apple's foldable borrows features Android makers, especially Samsung, have offered for years, so it isn't innovative.
Some mock Apple users for celebrating long-standing Android perks as new, and say Apple has run out of its own ideas.
A few say copying is an industry-wide habit, not just Apple's, while others point to the high price and early-adopter risk.

elements.text: Example of the Slack digest, to show the format. Figures are illustrative and not guaranteed to be accurate. Data through 2026-10-05. Ask a follow-up: mention the app or message it.

examples.q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
examples.a:
Small channels break out most. 37.1% of their videos outperformed their baseline (n=62 videos), against 18.4% for mid-size channels (n=38) and 0% for large ones (n=17). Average relative lift follows the same order: 6.42 for small, 1.11 for mid, and 0.54 for large.

Audiences are moderately happy everywhere, and mid-size channels are happiest:
- Small: net sentiment +14.5 (43.9% positive, 29.3% negative, n=846 product-side comments)
- Mid: +22 (47.8% positive, 25.5% negative, n=490)
- Large: +10 (39.2% positive, 28.8% negative, n=222)

Caveat: the large-channel group is small (17 videos), so treat its 0% rate cautiously. Small channels' high average lift may also be pulled up by a few big hits. These are associations, not causes.
examples.sql: WITH vids AS (SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size, p.outperformer, p.rel_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'), lift AS (SELECT size, COUNT(*) AS n_videos_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift FROM vids WHERE outperformer IS NOT NULL GROUP BY size), sent AS (SELECT v.size, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN vids v ON v.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY v.size) SELECT l.size, l.n_videos_with_baseline, l.outperformer_rate, l.avg_rel_lift, s.n_product_side, s.pct_positive, s.pct_negative, CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN s.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment FROM lift l LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size=l.size ORDER BY l.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
examples.a:
First impressions is the most reliable format for mid-sized channels. It has the largest sample (n=15) and a 33% outperformer rate (5 of 15), with an average relative lift of 1.42.

Explainer/tips has the highest average relative lift (1.91) and the same 33% rate, but that rests on only 3 videos (1 outperformer), so treat it as tentative.

Comparison is next at a 20% rate (1 of 5) and a 1.33 lift, also a small sample.

Keynote recap (n=4), upgrade advice (n=6), meme shorts (n=2), durability test (n=1) and "other" (n=2) had no outperformers. Their average lifts ran from 0.08 to 0.80, though most of those samples are tiny.

Caveat: these are associations from a small set of videos, not proof that format causes the results.
examples.sql: SELECT c.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(p.outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(p.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(p.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, ROUND(AVG(p.lift),3) AS avg_lift, SUM(CASE WHEN p.outperformer=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_outperformers FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' AND p.rel_lift IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
examples.a:
The two most negative high-lift videos are:

1. WSJ News, "I Tried Apple's First Folding iPhone. Here Are 3 Takeaways." (first impressions). Lift is 14.06 (relative lift 2.4). Net sentiment is -35, with 18% positive and 53% negative (n=17).

2. Both Sides of the Tech, "Apple Might Not Make Another iPhone Duo..." (upgrade advice). Lift is 29.77 (relative lift 5.1). Net sentiment is -27, with 27% positive and 55% negative (n=11).

Shawn Shaman's comparison video and Both Sides of the Tech's durability video are close behind, both at -25.

Caveat: each video has only 11 to 17 product-side comments, so these scores are rough. Lift and sentiment are also only associated, not causally linked.
examples.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT c.video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, AVG(c.sentiment='positive') AS pos, AVG(c.sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments c WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND c.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY c.video_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=10) SELECT ct.video_id, ct.title, cr.name AS creator_name, ct.format, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pos,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.neg,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(s.pos-s.neg,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content ct JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=ct.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=ct.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=ct.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, p.rel_lift DESC LIMIT 10

examples.q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
examples.a:
Largest topics: "Excitement and durability tests" leads (n=297, 18.9% of topic comments), then "Praise for the review" (n=267, 17.0%) and "Price and value" (n=184, 11.7%).

Fastest growing this week: Excitement and durability tests is first in absolute gain, rising from 29 to 160 comments (+131, up about 452%). Price and value is second (22 to 106, up about 382%), and the Samsung Fold comparison is third (17 to 88, up about 418%). By percentage alone, Apple copying Android accusations (7 to 47, up about 571%) and Folding animation praise (6 to 38, up about 533%) rise fastest, but from small bases.

Inner screen and crease and Duo comparisons and video content are growing slowest.

Caveat: this is a comment sample, and small starting counts make the percentages jumpy.
examples.sql: WITH sc AS (SELECT c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT max(d) AS m FROM sc), agg AS (SELECT sc.topic_id, count(*) AS n_total, sum(CASE WHEN d>m-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, sum(CASE WHEN d<=m-7 AND d>m-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prev_week FROM sc, mx WHERE sc.topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY sc.topic_id) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, ROUND(1.0*a.n_total/SUM(a.n_total) OVER (),3) AS share_of_topic_comments, a.n_this_week, a.n_prev_week, a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week AS change_abs, CASE WHEN a.n_prev_week>0 THEN ROUND(1.0*(a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week)/a.n_prev_week,3) END AS growth_pct, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY a.n_total DESC) AS size_rank, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week DESC) AS growth_rank FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id ORDER BY a.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
examples.a:
Duo sits clearly above general event and "other" content but below the competitor foldable. Its net sentiment is +21 (46% positive, 26% negative, n=1,411 comments across 129 videos).

- Competitor foldable: +33 (50% positive, 18% negative), but only n=40 comments across 3 videos, so treat it as directional.
- iPhone 18 Pro: +17 (42% positive, 25% negative), but n=12 across 2 videos, too small to read much into.
- General event content: -9 (29% positive, 38% negative), n=86.
- Other: -12 (26% positive, 38% negative), n=65.

Duo is the only topic with a large sample, so its score is the most reliable. These figures come from a sample of comments and show associations, not causes.
examples.sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(DISTINCT c.video_id) AS n_videos, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN 'ok' ELSE 'n<10' END AS n_check FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY (c.topic='duo') DESC, n_product_side DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
examples.a:
Fans like the anticipation most, along with the folding animation. The "Excitement and durability tests" topic has a net sentiment of +34 (n=247; 52% positive, 17% negative). Folding animation praise is +30 (n=92; 54% positive, 24% negative).

Price and value draws the most criticism among the larger topics. Its net is +12 (n=157; 46% positive, 34% negative). The Samsung Fold comparison has the highest negative share, 37%, but a smaller n of 57 and a net of +14. Apple-copying accusations have the weakest net, +8 (n=52), also a small sample.

Caveat: every topic nets positive, and the same topics appear on both the liked and criticised lists. So these are relative differences, and the sentiment may be about the topic debate rather than the phone itself.
examples.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.summary, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(cm.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(cm.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg FROM comments cm JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=cm.video_id JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=cm.topic_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value') AND t.pool='product' GROUP BY t.topic_id, t.name, t.summary), r AS (SELECT *, ROUND(n_pos*1.0/n,3) AS pct_pos, ROUND(n_neg*1.0/n,3) AS pct_neg, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY n_pos DESC) AS rp, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY n_neg DESC) AS rn FROM c) SELECT 'liked' AS side, name, summary, n, n_pos, n_neg, pct_pos, pct_neg FROM r WHERE rp<=8 UNION ALL SELECT 'criticised' AS side, name, summary, n, n_pos, n_neg, pct_pos, pct_neg FROM r WHERE rn<=8 LIMIT 40
